title: Proper direct image preserves ambient sums of classical complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and $f:X\to Y$ a proper scheme morphism. Assume $e\geq0$ bounds all fibre dimensions after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work in ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded pro-étale derived categories, with total K-injective $Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For every small family $(K_s)_{s\in I}$ of complexes with classical cohomology, the canonical ambient coproduct comparison is invertible:
$$\bigoplus_{s\in I}Rf_*K_s\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*\bigl(\bigoplus_{s\in I}K_s\bigr).$$
Classical means [sk-def-pe-classical-definition], and the comparison is the map whose composite with the $s$-th coprojection is $Rf_*(\iota_s)$. The family may be empty; no common cohomological bound or cohomological-dimension assumption on a ground field is imposed.

source.place: Étale statements, direct sums from finite cohomological dimension; old split steps 11–12

proof.text: Set $c=2e$ and $G=Rf_*$. The module categories $\mathcal A_X,\mathcal A_Y$ are Grothendieck by the small-ringed-site theorem. The proper classical amplitude lemma gives a triangulated $G$, preservation of all lower bounds, and $G(L)\in D^{\le b+c}$ for every classical $L\in D^{\le b}$. It also gives preservation of arbitrary sums by the total étale direct image $E$, supplying the explicit hypothesis of the bounded classical transport lemma. That lemma gives closure of classical sheaves under sums (apply its closure assertion to degree-zero objects), closure of classical complexes under sums and truncations, and invertibility of the canonical comparison on every common finite interval.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer; assembly of the three extracted arguments, returned proof steps 1–12

proof.text: Fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. Apply the family truncation lemma with $\mathcal P$ the classical module sheaves, using the properties from step 1. Put $U_s=\tau_{\le m}K_s$, $V_s=\tau_{\ge m-c}U_s$, and denote their maps by $u_s:U_s\to K_s$, $v_s:U_s\to V_s$. It gives all four isomorphisms $H^m(G(\bigoplus u_s))$, $H^m(G(\bigoplus v_s))$, $H^m(\bigoplus Gu_s)$ and $H^m(\bigoplus Gv_s)$, and places every $V_s$ in the common interval $[m-c,m]$.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer; assembly of the three extracted arguments, returned proof steps 1–12

proof.text: Write $\sigma_T:\bigoplus_sGT_s\to G(\bigoplus_sT_s)$ for the canonical comparison. For any family $h_s:T_s\to T'_s$, the coproduct universal property gives $G(\bigoplus h_s)\sigma_T=\sigma_{T'}(\bigoplus Gh_s)$: both composites with the $s$-th coprojection are $G(\iota'_sh_s)$. Apply this identity to $u$ and $v$. After $H^m$, the four maps from step 2 are invertible. The bounded classical transport lemma makes $\sigma_V$ invertible. Cancellation in the square for $v$ gives invertibility of $H^m(\sigma_U)$; cancellation in the square for $u$ then gives invertibility of $H^m(\sigma_K)$.

source.place: Étale statements and Transfer; assembly of the three extracted arguments, returned proof steps 1–12

proof.text: Since $m$ is arbitrary, the unbounded derived cohomology criterion makes $\sigma_K$ invertible. Its components are $G(\iota_s)$ by its defining universal property, so it is precisely the comparison in the statement. The empty family is covered by the same argument; equivalently, additive $G$ takes zero to zero.
